source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 768 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-768.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 768 was established by Ordinance No. 26928, passed by the Dallas City Council on September 26, 2007. (Ord. 26928)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-768.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 768 is established on property located at the northwest corner of Davis Street and Stevens Village Drive. The size of PD 768 is approximately 8.83 acres. (Ord. 26928)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-768.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this article:

(1) INTEGRATED RENEWABLE ENERGY SYSTEM means an accessory electrical power system for on-site generation and consumption that is mounted on the roof of a main structure.

(2) INTERIOR SIDE YARD means a side yard that is not adjacent to a street.

(3) ROOFTOP DECK means a flat surface similar to a floor located on the roof of a structure.

(4) STOOP means a small porch leading to the entrance of a residential structure.

(5) TANDEM PARKING means a parking layout where access to the front parking space is through a parking space that is directly behind it.

(6) WIND TURBINE means an accessory wind-driven turbine for generating electricity.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. 26928)

sections.title: Exhibits
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-768.104. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibit is incorporated into this article: Exhibit 768A: conceptual plan. (Ord. 26928)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-768.105. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit 768A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 26928)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-768.106. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) Except as provided in this section, a development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in this district.

(b) For single-family residential uses, a final plat may serve as the development plan. (Ord. 26928)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-768.107. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted in this district are those main uses permitted in the MF-2(A) Multifamily District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the MF-2(A) Multifamily District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the MF-2(A) Multifamily District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the MF-2(A) Multifamily District is subject to DIR in this district; etc.

(b) A private recreation center, club, or area is allowed by right.

(c) In Tract 4, the following main uses are permitted by right and only at street level:

-- Dry cleaning or laundry store. -- General merchandise or food store 3,500 square feet or less. -- Office. -- Personal service uses. -- Restaurant without drive-in or drive-through service. (Ord. 26928)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-768.108. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A- 4.217.

(b) An integrated renewable energy system and a wind turbine are permitted only in Tracts 2 and 4.

(c) The following accessory uses are not permitted:

-- Accessory outside display of merchandise. -- Accessory outside sales. -- Accessory pathological waste incinerator. (Ord. 26928)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-768.109. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A- 4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general.

(1) Setbacks.

(A) Setbacks from the Property lines must be provided as shown on the conceptual plan.

(B) Window sills, bay windows, belt courses, cornices, retaining walls no higher than 30 inches above grade, other architectural features, and chimneys may project up to three feet into the required front, side, or rear yards.

(C) Unenclosed balconies, unenclosed patios, cantilevered roof eaves, awnings, stairs, and stoops may project up to five feet into the required front, side, or rear yards if the width of the encroachment is no greater than 12 feet for any one encroachment.

(2) Density. Maximum number of dwelling units is 125.

(3) Height.

(A) Structures on top of a building. Except as provided in Subparagraph (C), the following structures may project a maximum of 12 feet above the maximum structure height:

(i) Elevator/stair penthouse or bulkhead.

(ii) Mechanical equipment room.

(iii) Cooling tower.

(iv) Tank designed to hold liquids.

(v) Ornamental cupola or dome.

(vi) Skylights.

(vii) Clerestory.

(viii) Visual screens which secure roof-mounted mechanical equipment.

(ix) Chimney and vent stacks.

(x) Amateur communications tower.

(xi) Parapet wall limited to a height of four feet above the roof line.

(B) Wind turbines and integrated renewable energy systems.

(i) Tract 2. Maximum wind turbine height is 30 feet above grade.

(ii) Tract 4. Wind turbines and integrated renewable energy systems mounted on the roof of a structure may project a maximum of 16 feet above the maximum structure height if the total structure height will not exceed 70 feet above grade.

(C) Residential proximity slope.

(i) In general.

(aa) Residential proximity slope originates from an R, R(A), D, D(A), TH, or TH(A) district.

(bb) Except for chimneys, structures listed in Subparagraph
(A) may project through the residential proximity slope to a height not to exceed the maximum structure height, or 12 feet above the residential proximity slope, whichever is less. Chimneys may project through a residential proximity slope to a height 12 feet above the residential proximity slope and 12 feet above the maximum structure height.

(ii) Tract 1. Residential proximity slope does not apply to single- family structures. If any portion of a non-single-family structure is over 30 feet in height, that portion of the structure may not be located above a one-to-two residential proximity slope.

(iii) Tract 2. Residential proximity slope does not apply.

(iv) Tracts 3 and 4. Except as provided in Subparagraph (B), if any structure exceeds 30 feet in height, that portion of the structure may not be located above a one-to-two residential proximity slope.

(b) Tract 1.

(1) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(2) Side and rear yard.

(A) No minimum side yard is required, except that a minimum separation of six feet is required between each main structure.

(B) Minimum rear yard is five feet.

(3) Height. Except as provided in Subsection (a)(3):

(A) for single-family uses, maximum structure height is 36 feet; and

(B) for all other uses, maximum structure height is 42 feet.

(4) Lot coverage.

(A) If the total lot coverage for the Property does not exceed 70 percent, the maximum lot coverage for each individual lot is 80 percent. Otherwise, maximum lot coverage for each individual lot is 60 percent.

(B) Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(5) Lot size. Minimum lot size is 1,000 square feet.

(6) Stories. Maximum number of stories above grade is three.

(c) Tract 2.

(1) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(2) Side and rear yard. Minimum side and rear yards are five feet, except that for lots with single-family uses, no minimum interior side yard is required.

(3) Height. Except as provided in Subsection (a)(3), maximum structure height is 42 feet.

(4) Lot coverage.

(A) If total lot coverage for the Property does not exceed 70 percent, the maximum lot coverage for each individual lot is 80 percent. Otherwise, maximum lot coverage for each individual lot is 60 percent.

(B) Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(5) Lot size. Minimum lot size is 1,000 square feet.

(6) Stories. Maximum number of stories above grade is three.

(d) Tract 3.

(1) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(2) Side and rear yard. Minimum side and rear yards are five feet, except that for lots with single-family uses no minimum interior side yard is required.

(3) Additional rooftop deck setback. An additional setback of 10 feet from the northern boundary of Tract 3 is required for a rooftop deck that is located on a structure exceeding one story in height in the area shown on the conceptual plan.

(4) Height. Except as provided on the conceptual plan and in Subsection (a)(3), maximum structure height is 42 feet.

(5) Lot coverage.

(A) If total lot coverage for the Property does not exceed 70 percent, the maximum lot coverage for each individual lot is 80 percent. Otherwise, maximum lot coverage for each individual lot is 60 percent.

(B) Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(6) Lot size. Minimum lot size 1,000 square feet.

(7) Stories. Except in the area shown on the conceptual plan, maximum number of stories above grade is three.

(e) Tract 4.

(1) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(2) Side and rear yard. Minimum side and rear yards are 10 feet.

(3) Floor area. For street-level uses, maximum floor area for each use is 2,000 square feet with a maximum total floor area for street-level uses of 30,000 square feet.

(4) Height.

(A) Except as provided in Subsection (a)(3), if a structure is developed with mixed uses, maximum structure height is 70 feet. Mixed uses means residential and non-residential uses with least 75 percent of the street-level floor area for non-residential uses, excluding structured, underground, or partially underground parking.

(B) Except as provided in Subsection (a)(3), if a structure is not developed with mixed uses, maximum structure height is 60 feet.

(5) Lot coverage.

(A) Maximum lot coverage is 80 percent.

(B) Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(6) Lot size. For single-family uses, minimum lot size is 1,000 square feet. For all other uses, minimum lot size for the MF-3(A) Multifamily District applies.

(7) Stories. Maximum number of stories above grade is six. (Ord. 26928)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-768.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general.

(1) Consult use regulations. Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(2) On-street parking credit. Required parking for non-residential uses and guest parking for single-family uses may be reduced by one space for every parallel parking space adjacent to the use in the Stevens Village Drive right-of-way. To receive credit, parking spaces must be marked in accordance with city regulations and are subject to the following restrictions:

(A) An on-street parking space may not be used to reduce the required parking for more than one use, except that an on-street parking space may be used to reduce the combined total parking requirement for a mixed-use project.

(B) An on-street parking space that is not available to the public at all times of the day may only be counted as a partial parking space in proportion to the amount of time that it is available. For example, a parking space that is available to the public only eight hours per day will be counted as one-third of a parking space (8 ÷ 24 = one-third). The total of the limited availability parking spaces will be counted to the nearest whole number, with one-half counted as an additional space.

(C) On-street guest parking for single-family uses may not be located more than 200 feet from the use requiring the guest parking.

(D) For non-residential uses, on-street parking spaces may not be located more than 500 feet from the use and not more than 50 percent of the required parking may be on-street.

(3) Parking structures. Parking structures must be located underground or have a facade that is similar in materials, architecture, and appearance to the facade of the main structure or the adjacent structure, except that breaks in the exterior parking structure facade not exceeding 40 feet in width are permitted at driveway and entryway locations. Openings in a parking structure facade may not exceed 50 percent of the total parking structure facade area.

(b) Tract 1. A minimum of two off-street parking spaces are required for each dwelling unit. Tandem parking is permitted only for resident parking.

(c) Tracts 2 and 3.

(1) A minimum of two off-street parking spaces are required for each dwelling unit.

(2) In a shared access development, guest parking must be provided at a ratio of one parking space for every eight dwelling units.

(3) Tandem parking is permitted only for resident parking.

(d) Tract 4.

(1) A minimum of one off-street parking space is required for each dwelling unit with one or fewer bedrooms, a minimum of one-and-one-half off-street parking spaces are required for each dwelling unit with two bedrooms, and a minimum of two off-street parking spaces are required for each dwelling unit with more than two bedrooms.

(2) Tandem parking is permitted only for resident parking.

(3) Surface parking is prohibited within 30 feet of Davis Street and Stevens Village Drive.

(4) Shared parking for mixed uses may be adjusted based on the following table. The adjusted standard off-street parking requirement is the largest of the five “time-of-day” column sums.

Shared Parking Table (for calculating adjusted standard parking requirements)

Use Category Morning Noon Afternoon Late Afternoon Evening

Residential 80% 60% 60% 70% 100%

Office related 100% 80% 100% 85% 35%

Retail related 60% 75% 70% 65% 70%

Bar and 20% 100% 30% 30% 100% restaurant

Other 100% 100% 100% 100% 100% (Ord. 26928)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-768.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, see Article VI.

(b) LEED certification. If a United States Green Building Council’s Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) certification for single-family and low-rise multifamily structures is available when the Property is developed, the following provisions apply:

(1) A LEED checklist, effective May 1, 2004 (or more current), must be submitted with an application for a building permit for development, indicating how the development will comply with a LEED compliance designation. A LEED accredited professional designated by the department of development services must affirm that development plans submitted for a building permit are LEED compliant. The building official must determine that the project is consistent with the standards and criteria for a LEED certified designation before a building permit may be issued.

(2) If during development, the developer is unable to achieve all of the green building rating system points identified on the checklist, the developer must replace any points not achieved with other green building rating system points acceptable under the United States Green Building Council’s LEED rating system.

(3) All supporting documentation and templates related to the points previously approved by the city for the LEED level designation must be submitted with an application for a certificate of occupancy. A certificate of occupancy may not be issued until a LEED accredited professional designated by the department of development services affirms that the building complies with the LEED certified designation. (Ord. 26928)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-768.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) In general.

(1) Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X. If there is a conflict between this section and Article X, this section controls.

(2) A mandatory perimeter landscape buffer strip is not required between lots or tracts.

(3) The Property is considered one lot for tree mitigation purposes.

(b) Parkway trees.

(1) Location. Except for Oak Cliff Boulevard, parkway trees must be located within the tree planting zone, which is the area parallel to and between two-and-one-half and 10 feet from the back of the street curb. Trees planted within the tree planting zone may count toward the total number of required site trees.

(2) Number.

(A) Davis Street and Stevens Village Drive. The minimum number of required parkway trees is determined by dividing the number of feet of street frontage, exclusive of visibility triangles, by 35. Fractions are rounded to the nearest whole number, with 0.5 being rounded up to the next higher whole number.

(B) Oak Cliff Boulevard. A minimum of eight parkway trees must be provided in the locations shown on the conceptual plan. A minimum of four of the parkway trees must be large trees.

(3) Type. Parkway trees must be recommended for local area use by the building official.

(4) Height and caliper.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph, parkway trees must have a minimum height of 12 feet and a minimum caliper of three-and-one-half inches measured at a point 12 inches above the root ball at the time of installation.

(B) On Stevens Village Drive, parkway trees may have a minimum height of six feet and a minimum caliper of two inches measured at a point 12 inches above the root ball at the time of installation if the building official determines that a parkway tree with a minimum height of 12 feet will interfere with utilities.

(5) Spacing. Parkway trees must be spaced as uniformly as practicable, but must be within 30 feet of the trunk of another required tree, exclusive of visibility triangles and driveways.

(c) Required site and parking lot trees.

(1) Type. Required site and parking lot trees must be recommended for local area use by the building official.

(2) Spacing.

(A) Required site and parking lot trees must be spaced as uniformly as practicable, but must be within 50 feet of the trunk of another required tree.

(B) Large trees may not be spaced closer than 20 feet from another large tree, 12 feet from a small tree, and 12 feet from a structure.

(C) Small trees may not be spaced closer than six feet from a structure.

(d) Tree grates. A tree grate is required if a tree is planted within two-and-one-half feet from a paved surface.

(e) Sidewalks.

(1) A minimum six-foot-wide sidewalk with at least four feet of unobstructed width must be provided along Davis Street and Stevens Village Drive. Tree grates may not be counted towards the minimum unobstructed sidewalk width.

(2) Sidewalks must be parallel to and within two-and-one-half feet to 15 feet from the back of the projected street curb. If the sidewalk is located within the front yard, the property owner must dedicate a sidewalk easement to the city to assure its availability to the public as a permanent pedestrian way.

(f) Maintenance. Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition.

(g) Private license granted.

(1) The city council hereby grants a revocable, non-exclusive license to the owners or tenants (with the written consent of the owner) of all property in this district for the exclusive purpose of authorizing compliance with the parkway landscaping requirements of this article. An owner or tenant is not required to pay an initial or annual fee for this license, although a fee may be charged for issuance of a parkway landscape permit. This private license will not terminate at the end of any specific period, however, the city council reserves the right to terminate this license at will, by resolution passed by the city council, any time such termination becomes necessary. The determination by the city council of the need for termination is final and binding. The city shall become entitled to possession of the licensed area without giving any notice and without the necessity of legal proceedings to obtain possession when, in its judgment, the purpose or use of the license is inconsistent with the public use of the right-of-way or when the purpose or use of the license is likely to become a nuisance or a threat to public safety. Upon termination of the license by the city council, each owner or tenant shall remove all improvements and installations in the public rights-of-way to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation.

(2) An owner or tenant is not required to comply with any landscaping requirement to the extent that compliance is made impossible due to the city council's revocation of the private license granted by this subsection.

(3) Upon the installation of landscaping and related amenities, such as irrigation systems, in the public rights-of-way, the owner or tenant shall procure, pay for, and keep in full force and effect commercial general liability insurance coverage with an insurance company authorized to do business in the State of Texas and otherwise acceptable to the city, covering, but not limited to, the liability assumed under the private license granted under this subsection, with combined single limits of liability for bodily injury and property damage of not less than $1,000,000 for each occurrence, and $2,000,000 annual aggregate. Coverage under this liability policy must be on an occurrence basis and the city shall be named as additional insured. Proof of such insurance must be sent to: Office of Risk Management, City of Dallas, 1500 Marilla, Dallas, Texas 75201, and the policy must provide for 30 days prior written notice to the Office of Risk Management of cancellation, expiration, non-renewal, or material change in coverage. All subrogation rights for loss or damage against the city are hereby waived to the extent that they are covered by this liability insurance policy.

(4) Each owner or tenant is responsible for maintaining the landscaping in a healthy, growing condition, for keeping related amenities in good repair and condition, and for keeping the premises safe and from deteriorating in value or condition, at no expense to the city. The city is absolutely exempt from any requirements to make repairs or to maintain the landscaping, related amenities, or the premises. The granting of a license for landscaping and related amenities under this subsection does not release the owner or tenant from liability for the installation or maintenance of trees, landscaping, and related amenities in the public right-of-way.

(h) Parkway landscape permit.

(1) It is the responsibility of the property owner to apply for and obtain a parkway landscape permit before locating trees, landscaping, or related amenities in the parkway. An application

for a parkway landscape permit must be made to the director. The application must be in writing on a form approved by the director and accompanied by plans or drawings showing the area of the parkway affected and the planting or other amenities proposed.

(2) Upon receipt of the application and any required fees, the director shall circulate it to all affected city departments and utilities for review and comment. If, after receiving comments from affected city departments and utilities, the director determines that the construction, planting, or other amenities proposed will not be inconsistent with and will not unreasonably impair the public use of the right-of-way, the director shall issue a parkway landscape permit to the property owner; otherwise, the director shall deny the permit.

(3) A property owner is not required to comply with any parkway landscaping requirement of this article if compliance is made impossible due to the director's denial of a parkway landscape permit.

(4) A parkway landscape permit issued by the director is subject to immediate revocation upon written notice if at any time the director determines that the use of the parkway authorized by the permit is inconsistent with or unreasonably impairs the public use of the right-of-way. The property owner is not required to comply with any parkway landscaping requirement of this section if compliance is made impossible due to the director's revocation of a parkway landscape permit.

(5) The issuance of a parkway landscape permit under this subsection does not excuse the property owner, his agents, or employees from liability for the installation or maintenance of trees or other amenities in the public right-of-way. (Ord. 26928)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-768.113. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 26928)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-768.114. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) A shared access development is exempt from the limitations on the minimum and maximum number of lots in Section 51A-4.411(c)(1). (Ord. 26928)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-768.115. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this district until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 26928)

sections.text:
